findings.description: The bucket has no ACL or public-access-block configuration and is explicitly commented as public, allowing unauthenticated or unauthorized access to stored data, including a sensitive customer master file uploaded to it.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects (including sensitive customer master data) are stored unencrypted at rest.

Versioning is not enabled on this bucket, so combined with public access and no logging, unauthorized modifications or deletions of objects like the customer master file cannot be detected or recovered.

findings.issue_category: sensitive data in unencrypted public bucket
findings.description: A customer master spreadsheet containing likely sensitive customer data is uploaded to aws_s3_bucket.data, which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing sensitive data to unauthorized parties.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in the operations bucket are stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in the data-science bucket are stored unencrypted at rest.
